messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State

### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Finish the world, interiors, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.
- Test the game in-browser, resolve runtime issues, capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports missing `js/interiors.js`.
- Gameplay modules and startup are not implemented.

## Next Move
1. Create `js/interiors.js` and complete `js/world.js`.
2. Implement and connect the remaining playable systems, including `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports missing `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Finish the world, interiors, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports missing `js/interiors.js`.
- Gameplay modules and startup are not implemented.

## Next Move
1. Create `js/interiors.js` and complete `js/world.js`.
2. Implement and connect the remaining playable systems, including `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports missing `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Finish the world, interiors, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports missing `js/interiors.js`.
- Gameplay modules and startup are not implemented.

## Next Move
1. Create `js/interiors.js` and complete `js/world.js`.
2. Implement and connect the remaining playable systems, including `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports missing `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Finish the world, interiors, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports missing `js/interiors.js`.
- Gameplay modules and startup are not implemented.

## Next Move
1. Create `js/interiors.js` and complete `js/world.js`.
2. Implement and connect the remaining playable systems, including `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports missing `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls.
- Finish implementation and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Implement `js/interiors.js` and complete `js/world.js`.
- Implement and connect remaining gameplay systems, including `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports `js/interiors.js`, which is not yet present; an agent has been assigned to implement it.

## Next Move
1. Continue once `js/interiors.js` implementation is available; review its integration with `js/world.js`.
2. Complete world, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls.
- Finish implementation and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Implement `js/interiors.js` and complete `js/world.js`.
- Implement and connect remaining gameplay systems, including `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports `./interiors.js`, which is not yet present; an agent was assigned to implement it.

## Next Move
1. Continue once `js/interiors.js` is available; review integration with `js/world.js`.
2. Complete world, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls, and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Implement `js/interiors.js` and complete `js/world.js`.
- Implement and connect remaining gameplay systems, including `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports `./interiors.js`, which is not yet present; an agent was assigned to implement it.

## Next Move
1. Continue once `js/interiors.js` is available; review integration with `js/world.js`.
2. Complete world, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Casebook

Tab opens the case file: evidence, suspects, map, the sect, notes. You can fast-travel to known locations from the map.

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

128:

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

129:

Stay human

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls, and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Implement `js/interiors.js` and complete `js/world.js`.
- Implement and connect remaining gameplay systems, including `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports `./interiors.js`, which is not yet present; an agent was assigned to implement it.

## Next Move
1. Continue once `js/interiors.js` is available; review integration with `js/world.js`.
2. Complete world, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls, and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Complete `js/world.js` and integrate interior scenes.
- Implement remaining gameplay systems, including controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports `./interiors.js`, which is not yet present; an agent is working on it.

## Next Move
1. Continue once `js/interiors.js` is available; review integration with `js/world.js`.
2. Complete world, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `js/world.js` has not yet been fully inspected; its visible exports include `World` and `std`, and it initializes `interactables` and `interactablesById`.

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls, and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Complete `js/world.js` and integrate interior scenes.
- Implement remaining gameplay systems, including controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports `./interiors.js`, which was not present in the last inspected state; an agent was working on it.

## Next Move
1. Check whether `js/interiors.js` is available and integrate it with `js/world.js`.
2. Complete world, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `js/world.js` has not been fully inspected; its visible exports include `World` and `std`, and it initializes `interactables` and `interactablesById`.

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls, and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Complete `js/world.js` and integrate interior scenes.
- Implement remaining gameplay systems, including controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports `./interiors.js`, which was not present in the last inspected state; an agent was working on it.

## Next Move
1. Check whether `js/interiors.js` is available and integrate it with `js/world.js`.
2. Complete world, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `js/world.js` has not been fully inspected; its visible exports include `World` and `std`, and it initializes `interactables` and `interactablesById`.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls, and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Complete `js/world.js` and integrate interior scenes.
- Implement remaining gameplay systems, including controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports `./interiors.js`, which was not present in the last inspected file listing; its availability is unconfirmed.

## Next Move
1. Check whether `js/interiors.js` is available and integrate it with `js/world.js`.
2. Complete world, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `js/world.js` has not been fully inspected; its visible exports include `World` and `std`, and it initializes `interactables` and `interactablesById`.

Work the scene

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls, and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Complete `js/world.js` and integrate interior scenes.
- Implement remaining gameplay systems, including controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports `./interiors.js`, but that file was absent from the latest `js/*` listing.

## Next Move
1. Check whether `js/interiors.js` is available; create or integrate it as needed.
2. Complete world, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `js/world.js` was only partially inspected; its visible exports include `World` and `std`, and it initializes `interactables` and `interactablesById`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls, and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Complete `js/world.js` and integrate interior scenes.
- Implement remaining gameplay systems, including controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports `./interiors.js`, but its availability has not been confirmed.

## Next Move
1. Check whether `js/interiors.js` exists; create or integrate it as needed.
2. Complete world, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `js/world.js` was only partially inspected; its visible exports include `World` and `std`, and it initializes `interactables` and `interactablesById`.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls, and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Complete `js/world.js` and integrate interior scenes.
- Implement remaining gameplay systems, including controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports `./interiors.js`, but that file’s availability has not been confirmed; the latest file listing did not include it.

## Next Move
1. Check whether `js/interiors.js` exists; create or integrate it as needed.
2. Complete world, controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and startup.
3. Run and verify the game, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `js/world.js` was only partially inspected; its visible exports include `World` and `std`, and it initializes `interactables` and `interactablesById`.

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Casebook

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls, and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.
- Inspected `js/world.js`, `index.html`, `js/lore.js`, and `js/util.js`; found the world module has substantial environment-building code through `_initWeather()`.

### Active
- Complete `js/world.js` and integrate interior scenes.
- Implement remaining gameplay systems, including controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports `./interiors.js`, but that file is absent from the current `js/` listing.

## Next Move
1. Create or integrate `js/interiors.js` to satisfy `buildInteriors(this)`.
2. Inspect and complete the rest of `js/world.js`, then implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports missing `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `js/world.js` initializes the renderer, environment, town, props, weather, and NPC meshes; visible exports include `World` and `std`.
- The `js/` directory currently contains `audio.js`, `lore.js`, `util.js`, and `world.js`; no `interiors.js` or `main.js` was found.

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls, and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient autonomous killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Confirmed `SCENE_ANCHORS` and `KEY_PLACES` are exported from `js/lore.js`.

### Active
- Complete `js/world.js` and integrate interior scenes.
- Implement remaining gameplay systems: controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` imports `./interiors.js`, but that file is absent from `js/`.

## Next Move
1. Create `js/interiors.js` to satisfy `buildInteriors(this)`.
2. Inspect and complete `js/world.js`, then implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser, resolve errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports missing `./interiors.js`.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `js/world.js` initializes the renderer, environment, town, props, weather, and NPC meshes; visible exports include `World` and `std`.
- The `js/` directory currently contains `audio.js`, `lore.js`, `util.js`, and `world.js`; no `interiors.js` or `main.js` was found.

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

## Objective
- Build and verify a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Added `js/interiors.js` during the latest work; it now appears in the project and may resolve the missing-import blocker, but its implementation has not been inspected or verified.

### Active
- Complete `js/world.js` and integrate interior scenes.
- Implement remaining gameplay systems: controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Run and verify the game in-browser and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- No confirmed blocker; inspect the newly present `js/interiors.js` and resolve any integration issues.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `js/interiors.js` and the remainder of `js/world.js`; confirm interior APIs and complete world update/navigation behavior.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run the game in-browser, fix errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `buildInteriors` from `./interiors.js`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Newly present interior-scene module; implementation and compatibility need verification.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, while `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` initializes renderer, environment, town, props, weather, and NPC meshes; visible exports include `World` and `std`.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was not present in the last project listing.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world module.
- Added `js/interiors.js`; implementation and compatibility remain unverified.

### Active
- Complete `js/world.js` and integrate interior scenes.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Run and verify the game in-browser, fix errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- No confirmed blocker.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `js/interiors.js` and the remainder of `js/world.js`; confirm interior APIs and complete world update/navigation behavior.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run the game in-browser, fix errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `buildInteriors` from `./interiors.js`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior-scene module, not yet inspected or verified.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, while `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` initializes renderer, environment, town, props, weather, and NPC meshes; visible exports include `World` and `std`.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was not present in the last project listing.

How to Investigate

123:
124:

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

125:

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

126:

Casebook

Tab opens the case file: evidence, suspects, map, the sect, notes. You can fast-travel to known locations from the map.

127:

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

128:

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

129:

Stay human

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

## Objective
- Build and verify a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world and interior modules.

### Active
- Verify `js/interiors.js` APIs and complete `js/world.js` navigation/update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete `js/interiors.js` and `js/world.js` implementations; confirm their APIs and finish world navigation/update behavior.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `buildInteriors` from `./interiors.js`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior-scene module; implementation and compatibility unverified.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, while `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.
- `World` initializes renderer, environment, town, props, weather, and NPC meshes; visible exports include `World` and `std`.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build and verify a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world and interior modules.

### Active
- Verify `js/interiors.js` APIs and complete `js/world.js` navigation/update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix errors, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete `js/interiors.js` and `js/world.js` implementations; confirm their APIs and finish world navigation/update behavior.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `buildInteriors` from `./interiors.js`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior-scene module; implementation and compatibility unverified.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, while `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.
- `World` initializes renderer, environment, town, props, weather, and NPC meshes; visible exports include `World` and `std`.
- `js/interiors.js` imports `LOCATIONS`; its viewed implementation was truncated, with only lines 190–210 inspected.

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Casebook

Tab opens the case file: evidence, suspects, map, the sect, notes. You can fast-travel to known locations from the map.

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

## Objective
- Build and verify a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world and interior modules.
- Inspected portions of `js/world.js`, `js/interiors.js`, `js/lore.js`, and `js/audio.js`; full implementations and APIs remain unverified.

### Active
- Verify `js/interiors.js` APIs and complete `js/world.js` navigation/update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete `js/interiors.js` and `js/world.js` implementations; confirm their APIs and finish world navigation/update behavior.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `buildInteriors` from `./interiors.js`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior-scene module; implementation and compatibility unverified.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, while `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.
- `World` initializes renderer, environment, town, props, weather, and NPC meshes; visible exports include `World` and `std`.

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world and interior modules.
- Inspected portions of `js/world.js`, `js/interiors.js`, `js/lore.js`, and `js/audio.js`.

### Active
- Verify `js/interiors.js` APIs and complete `js/world.js` navigation/update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete `js/interiors.js` and `js/world.js`; confirm their APIs and finish world navigation/update behavior.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `buildInteriors` from `./interiors.js`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior-scene module; implementation and compatibility unverified.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, while `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.
- `World` initializes renderer, environment, town, props, weather, and NPC meshes; visible exports include `World` and `std`.
- `js/lore.js` exports `LOCATIONS`, `SCENE_ANCHORS`, `KEY_PLACES`, and other setting data.

## Objective
- Build and verify a complete, playable psychological horror detective game, **THE NINTH HOUR**, set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Use original fictional lore and cases; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world and interior modules.
- Inspected portions of `js/world.js`, `js/interiors.js`, `js/lore.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/util.js`, and `index.html`.

### Active
- Verify `js/interiors.js` APIs and complete `js/world.js` navigation/update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete `js/interiors.js` and `js/world.js`; confirm their APIs and finish world navigation/update behavior.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `buildInteriors` from `./interiors.js`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior-scene module; implementation and compatibility unverified.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, while `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.
- `World` initializes renderer, environment, town, props, weather, and NPC meshes; visible exports include `World` and `std`.
- `js/lore.js` exports `LOCATIONS`, `SCENE_ANCHORS`, `KEY_PLACES`, and other setting data.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world and interior modules.
- Inspected portions of `js/world.js`, `js/interiors.js`, `js/lore.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/util.js`, and `index.html`.

### Active
- Verify `js/interiors.js` APIs and complete `js/world.js` navigation/update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete `js/interiors.js` and `js/world.js`; confirm their APIs and finish world navigation/update behavior.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `buildInteriors` from `./interiors.js`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior-scene module; implementation and compatibility unverified.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.
- `World` initializes renderer, environment, town, props, weather, and NPC meshes; visible exports include `World` and `std`.
- `js/lore.js` exports `LOCATIONS`, `SCENE_ANCHORS`, `KEY_PLACES`, and other setting data.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world and interior modules.
- Inspected `index.html`, `js/world.js`, `js/interiors.js`, `js/lore.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/util.js`, and `css/style.css`.

### Active
- Confirm `js/interiors.js` APIs and complete `js/world.js` navigation/update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete `js/interiors.js` and `js/world.js`; confirm their APIs and finish world navigation/update behavior.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `buildInteriors` from `./interiors.js`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior-scene module; implementation and compatibility unverified.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.
- `World` initializes renderer, environment, town, props, weather, and NPC meshes; visible exports include `World` and `std`.
- `js/lore.js` exports `LOCATIONS`, `SCENE_ANCHORS`, `KEY_PLACES`, and other setting data.

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Casebook

Tab opens the case file: evidence, suspects, map, the sect, notes. You can fast-travel to known locations from the map.

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world and interior modules.
- Inspected `index.html`, `js/world.js`, `js/interiors.js`, `js/lore.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/util.js`, and `css/style.css`.

### Active
- Confirm `js/interiors.js` APIs and complete `js/world.js` navigation/update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete `js/interiors.js` and `js/world.js`; confirm their APIs and finish world navigation/update behavior.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; imports `buildInteriors` from `./interiors.js`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior-scene module; implementation and compatibility unverified.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.
- `World` initializes renderer, environment, town, props, weather, and NPC meshes; visible exports include `World` and `std`.
- `js/lore.js` exports `LOCATIONS`, `SCENE_ANCHORS`, `KEY_PLACES`, and other setting data.

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Casebook

Tab opens the case file: evidence, suspects, map, the sect, notes. You can fast-travel to known locations from the map.

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

Stay human

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world and interior modules.
- Inspected `index.html`, `js/world.js`, `js/interiors.js`, `js/lore.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/util.js`, and `css/style.css`; full interior and world APIs remain unverified.

### Active
- Finish world navigation/update behavior and implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the remaining portions of `js/world.js` and `js/interiors.js`; confirm their APIs and complete world navigation/update behavior.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation importing `buildInteriors` from `./interiors.js`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior-scene module; implementation and compatibility need verification.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.
- `js/world.js` visibly exports `World` and `std`; `World` initializes renderer, environment, town, props, weather, and NPC meshes.
- `js/lore.js` exports `LOCATIONS`, `SCENE_ANCHORS`, `KEY_PLACES`, and other setting data.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world and interior modules.
- Inspected portions of `index.html`, `js/world.js`, `js/interiors.js`, `js/lore.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/util.js`, and `css/style.css`.

### Active
- Confirm world and interior APIs; finish world navigation and update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining portions of `js/world.js` and `js/interiors.js`; confirm their APIs and complete world navigation/update behavior.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior-scene module; implementation and compatibility need verification.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.
- Reads of `js/world.js` and `js/interiors.js` were truncated, so their full APIs remain unverified.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world and interior modules.
- Read the available portions of `index.html`, `js/world.js`, `js/interiors.js`, `js/lore.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/util.js`, and `css/style.css`; full APIs for the world and interiors remain unverified.

### Active
- Confirm world and interior APIs; finish world navigation and update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the remaining portions of `js/world.js` and `js/interiors.js`; confirm their APIs and complete world navigation/update behavior.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior-scene module; implementation and compatibility need verification.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world and interior modules.
- Inspected portions of `index.html`, `js/world.js`, `js/interiors.js`, `js/lore.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/util.js`, and `css/style.css`.

### Active
- Verify world and interior APIs; finish world navigation and update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining portions of `js/world.js` and `js/interiors.js`; confirm their APIs and complete world navigation/update behavior.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior-scene module; implementation and compatibility need verification.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.
