## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world and interior modules.

### Active
- Verify world and interior APIs; finish world navigation and update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining portions of `js/world.js` and `js/interiors.js`; confirm their APIs and complete world navigation/update behavior.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior-scene module; implementation and compatibility need verification.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.

4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.

8:

10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Completed `js/interiors.js` with interior layouts, evidence props, interactables, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- `js/interiors.js` passed `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Verify `js/world.js` APIs and complete world navigation/update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining `js/world.js` and confirm its API compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Completed interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Casebook

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Completed `js/interiors.js` with interior layouts, evidence props, interactables, and custom chapel undercroft geometry; `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Verify `js/world.js` APIs and complete world navigation/update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the remaining `js/world.js` implementation and confirm API compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.

Move

Work the scene

Casebook

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Completed `js/interiors.js` with 12 interior builders, layouts, evidence props, interactables registered in both collections, and custom chapel undercroft geometry; `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Verify `js/world.js` APIs and complete world navigation/update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the remaining `js/world.js` implementation and confirm API compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the last project listing.

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Casebook

Tab opens the case file: evidence, suspects, map, the sect, notes. You can fast-travel to known locations from the map.

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Completed `js/interiors.js` with 12 interior builders, layouts, evidence props, interactables registered in both collections, and custom chapel undercroft geometry; `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Verify `js/world.js` APIs and complete world navigation/update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `js/world.js` in full and confirm API compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the project listing.
- Recent inspection of `js/world.js` and `js/interiors.js` was truncated; no implementation or verification progress was made in that exchange.

How to Investigate

123:
124:

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

125:

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

126:

Casebook

Tab opens the case file: evidence, suspects, map, the sect, notes. You can fast-travel to known locations from the map.

127:

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

128:

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

129:

Stay human

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Completed `js/interiors.js` with 12 interior builders, layouts, evidence props, interactables registered in both collections, and custom chapel undercroft geometry; `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Verify `js/world.js` APIs and complete world navigation/update behavior.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `js/world.js` fully and confirm API compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which was absent from the project listing.
- Recent inspection of `js/world.js` and `js/interiors.js` was truncated; no implementation or verification progress was made in that exchange.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Completed `js/interiors.js` with 12 interior builders, layouts, evidence props, interactables registered in both collections, and custom chapel undercroft geometry; `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Confirm `js/world.js` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `js/world.js` fully and confirm API compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which is currently absent.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Completed `js/interiors.js` with 12 interior builders, layouts, evidence props, interactables registered in both collections, and custom chapel undercroft geometry; `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Confirm `js/world.js` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `js/world.js` fully and confirm API compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement the remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which is currently absent.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented `js/interiors.js` with 12 interior builders, layouts, evidence props, interactables registered in both collections, and custom chapel undercroft geometry; `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Inspected `js/world.js`, `js/lore.js`, `index.html`, and `js/interiors.js`; no API compatibility determination or implementation was recorded.

### Active
- Confirm `js/world.js` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `js/world.js` APIs and verify compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which is currently absent.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented `js/interiors.js` with 12 interior builders, layouts, evidence props, interactables registered in both collections, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed for the interior implementation.

### Active
- Confirm `js/world.js` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `js/world.js` APIs and verify compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which is currently absent.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented `js/interiors.js` with 12 interior builders, layouts, evidence props, interactables registered in both collections, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed for the interior implementation.

### Active
- Confirm `js/world.js` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `js/world.js` APIs and verify compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which is currently absent.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented `js/interiors.js` with 12 interior builders, layouts, evidence props, interactables registered in both collections, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed for the interior implementation.
- Inspected `js/world.js`, `js/lore.js`, `js/util.js`, `index.html`, and `js/interiors.js`.

### Active
- Confirm `js/world.js` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `js/world.js` APIs and verify compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement remaining gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `index.html` references `js/main.js`, which is currently absent.

input.prompt: Inspect js/world.js, js/interiors.js, js/lore.js, index.html, css/style.css, and audio.js. Report world class public APIs and likely compatibility issues, relevant UI element IDs, and a concise implementation plan for the missing gameplay/main.js. Do not edit files.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented `js/interiors.js` with 12 interior builders, layouts, evidence props, interactables registered in both collections, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed for the interior implementation.
- Inspected `js/world.js`, `js/lore.js`, `js/util.js`, `index.html`, `js/interiors.js`, `js/audio.js`, and `css/style.css`.
- Confirmed `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; the game has not yet been implemented or browser-tested.

### Active
- Confirm `js/world.js` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining `js/world.js` and `index.html` details, especially location entry, update/render behavior, and interface element IDs; resolve compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement the missing gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` currently exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers; no update/render/navigation methods have been confirmed yet.
- `js/interiors.js` indexes evidence in world coordinates and adds records to both `world.interactables` and `world.interactablesById`.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented `js/interiors.js` with 12 interior builders, layouts, evidence props, interactables registered in both collections, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed for the interior implementation.
- Inspected `js/world.js`, `js/lore.js`, `js/util.js`, `index.html`, `js/interiors.js`, `js/audio.js`, and `css/style.css`.
- Confirmed `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

### Active
- Confirm `js/world.js` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining `js/world.js` and `index.html` details, especially location entry, update/render behavior, and interface element IDs; resolve compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement the missing gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers; no update/render/navigation methods have been confirmed.
- `js/interiors.js` indexes evidence in world coordinates and adds records to both `world.interactables` and `world.interactablesById`.

Work the scene

Casebook

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented `js/interiors.js` with 12 interior builders, layouts, evidence props, interactables registered in both collections, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed for the interior implementation.
- Inspected `js/world.js`, `js/lore.js`, `js/util.js`, `index.html`, `js/interiors.js`, `js/audio.js`, and `css/style.css`.
- Confirmed `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

### Active
- Confirm `js/world.js` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining `js/world.js` and `index.html` details, especially location entry, update/render behavior, and interface element IDs; resolve compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement the missing gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers; no update/render/navigation methods have been confirmed.
- `index.html` is partially inspected; its interface element IDs and remaining `js/world.js` behavior still need inspection.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed for the interior implementation.

### Active
- Confirm `js/world.js` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement gameplay systems and `js/main.js`, which `index.html` references but which is missing.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining `js/world.js` and `index.html` details, especially location entry, update/render behavior, and interface element IDs; resolve compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers; update/render/navigation methods have not been confirmed.
- Gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed for the interior implementation.

### Active
- Confirm `js/world.js` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement gameplay systems and `js/main.js`, referenced by `index.html` but missing.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining `js/world.js` and `index.html` details, especially location entry, update/render behavior, and interface element IDs; resolve compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers; update/render/navigation methods have not been confirmed.
- Gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

125:

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Casebook

Tab opens the case file: evidence, suspects, map, the sect, notes. You can fast-travel to known locations from the map.

127:

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

128:

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

129:

Stay human

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed for the interior implementation.

### Active
- Confirm `js/world.js` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement gameplay systems and `js/main.js`, referenced by `index.html` but missing.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `js/world.js` navigation/update behavior and `index.html` interface IDs; check compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers; update/render/navigation methods have not been confirmed.
- Gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State

### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed for the interior implementation.

### Active
- Confirm `js/world.js` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement gameplay systems and `js/main.js`, referenced by `index.html` but missing.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `js/world.js` navigation/update behavior and `index.html` interface IDs; check compatibility with `js/interiors.js`.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`, imports `buildInteriors`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers; update/render/navigation methods have not been confirmed.
- Gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## `js/main.js` integration guidance

No `js/main.js` was found in the search, so this is a guide to building the entry point rather than a description of existing main-file behavior.

### Dependencies and startup order

- Import `World` from [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js). It already depends on the lore data, shared utilities, and `buildInteriors`, so the entry point should generally use `World` rather than reconstructing those pieces itself.
- Import `AudioEngine` from [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js).
- Use [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/lore.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/lore.js) for the exported `GAME_TITLE`, `TOWN`, and `LOCATIONS` data if the entry point needs to populate the page or present location-specific information.
- Load `css/style.css` for the interface styling. Its tokens and responsive patterns are intended to be reused rather than replaced with unrelated styles.

### World and interiors

## Findings

`index.html` loads `js/main.js` as an ES module, but that file is absent. The `js/` directory currently contains only `audio.js`, `interiors.js`, `lore.js`, `util.js`, and `world.js`. The game therefore has no entry point to wire up its UI, controls, or animation loop.

There is also a separate startup blocker: `World` calls `this._initNpcMeshes()` during construction, but the method is not defined in `world.js`. Instantiating `World` will throw at that call unless the method is added or the call is removed.

## `World` API

`World` is exported from `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`, along with the `std(color, rough, metal, extra)` material helper.

- **Construction and resize:** `new World()` creates a Three.js scene, camera, renderer, lights, ground, roads, town, props, interiors, and weather; `resize()` updates camera aspect and renderer dimensions.
- **Collision:** `addCollider(minX, maxX, minZ, maxZ, tag)`, `addColliderAt(x, z, w, d, tag)`, and `collides(x, z, r)` provide rectangular collision bounds and world-edge checks.
- **Geometry and signage:** `makeBox`, `makeCylinder`, `makePlane`, and `sign`.
- **Buildings and environment:** `makeSolidBuilding`, `addWindows`, `frontPos`, `makeEnterable`, `_wall`, `makeOutdoorZone`, `makeHouse`, `makeCar`, `makeCemetery`, `makeRiverbank`, `makeStreetLamp`, `makeTree`, `makeStreetFurniture`, plus initialization helpers for lights, ground, roads, town, props, and weather.
- **Useful state:** `scene`, `camera`, `renderer`, `colliders`, `interactables`, `interactablesById`, `interiors`, `buildingGroups`, `scenes`, `keyNpcs`, `genericNpc`, `genericList`, and environment fields such as `rain`, `snow`, `stars`, and `moon`.

There is **no apparent `World` update, animation, or render method**; the entry point will need to own the render loop and any frame updates. `buildInteriors(world)` in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/interiors.js` expects `scene`, an `interactables` array, and a Map-like `interactablesById`. It adds evidence objects with fields including `id`, `position`, `label`, `description`, `kind`, `location`, and `object`.

## UI and other modules

The main UI IDs in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html` are:

- **Scene and HUD:** `scene`, `hud`, `clock`, `weather`, `moon`, `objective`, `objective-title`, `objective-sub`, `meter-health`, `meter-stress`, `meter-stamina`, `val-health`, `val-stress`, `val-stamina`, `stress-word`, `tool-flash`, `crosshair`, `prompt`, `prompt-text`, `toasts`, `ticker`, `controls-hint`, `interact-progress`.
- **Title, help, and saves:** `title-screen`, `btn-start`, `btn-continue`, `btn-load`, `btn-help`, `help-modal`, `slots-modal`, `slots-title`, `slots-list`, `slots-mode`, `slots-close`, `slots-cancel`.
- **Casebook:** `casebook`, `nav-evidence`, `nav-suspects`, `book-clock`, `book-weather`, `book-close`, `page-eyebrow`, `page-title`, `paper-stamp`, `book-content`, `page-foot`.
- **Dialogue:** `dialogue`, `dlg-portrait`, `dlg-initials`, `dlg-name`, `dlg-role`, `dlg-mood`, `dlg-trust-bar`, `dlg-text`, `dlg-options`, `dlg-hint`, `dlg-leave`.
- **Pause and ending:** `pause`, `pause-resume`, `pause-save`, `pause-load`, `pause-help`, `pause-quit`, `opt-audio`, `opt-grain`, `ending-screen`, `ending-eyebrow`, `ending-title`, `ending-text`, `ending-stats`, `ending-restart`, `ending-titlebtn`.
- **Overlays:** `flash`, `dread`, `fade`, `hint-banner`.

`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js` exports `AudioEngine`; its main controls include `init`, `setScene`, `setStress`, `resume`, `setMuted`, and `tick`, plus effects such as `ui`, `shutter`, `stinger`, `bell`, `thunder`, and `scream`. `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/lore.js` provides the game title, locations, scene anchors, cast, and narrative data. `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/util.js` provides seeded RNG and shared utilities.

## Compatibility and startup risks

- Fix the missing `main.js` reference target before expecting the page to initialize.
- Resolve the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` call before constructing `World`.
- The project uses browser ES modules and imports Three.js 0.160 directly from jsDelivr. It needs a module-capable browser, network access to the CDN, and should be served over HTTP(S) rather than opened as a local file.
- `World` assumes browser globals such as `innerWidth` and `devicePixelRatio`, and assumes `#scene` exists.
- WebGL must be available for `WebGLRenderer`; Web Audio may require initialization or resumption from a user gesture.
- No `World` frame-update or render API is present, so the main loop must handle rendering and coordinate game updates.

## Concise `main.js` plan

1. Import `World`, `AudioEngine`, and the required lore/util modules; resolve the NPC initialization blocker before creating the world.
2. Set up game state, player movement and collision using `World.collides`, camera control, and the renderer’s animation loop.
3. Connect proximity/interactable handling to `world.interactables` and `world.interactablesById`, then wire objective, evidence, dialogue, casebook, and HUD updates to the existing IDs.
4. Bind title, pause, save/load, settings, and ending controls; initialize/resume audio in response to user input.
5. Handle resize and input cleanup, and update any weather or environment behavior that is not already animated by `World`.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed for the interior implementation.
- Inspected `js/world.js`, `index.html`, `js/util.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/lore.js`, and `js/interiors.js` for integration compatibility.
- Identified that `index.html` references a missing `js/main.js`, and `World` calls an undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` during construction.

### Active
- Confirm `World` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete `js/world.js` implementation and interface IDs in `index.html`; resolve the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup issue and verify interior compatibility.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.
- `World` construction currently calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

Casebook

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed for the interior implementation.
- Inspected `js/world.js`, `index.html`, `js/util.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/lore.js`, and `js/interiors.js` for integration compatibility.

### Active
- Confirm `World` APIs and navigation/update behavior work with `js/interiors.js`.
- Implement gameplay systems and `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete `js/world.js` implementation and interface IDs in `index.html`; resolve the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup issue and verify interior compatibility.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation; exports `World` and `std`.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed interior implementation passed `node --check` and `git diff --check`.
- Inspected `js/world.js`, `index.html`, `js/util.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/lore.js`, and `js/interiors.js` for integration compatibility.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed interior implementation passed `node --check` and `git diff --check`.
- Inspected `js/world.js`, `index.html`, `js/util.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/lore.js`, and `js/interiors.js` for integration compatibility.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed interior implementation passed `node --check` and `git diff --check`.
- Inspected `js/world.js`, `index.html`, `js/util.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/lore.js`, and `js/interiors.js` for integration compatibility.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, and custom chapel undercroft geometry.
- Confirmed interior implementation passed `node --check` and `git diff --check`.
- Inspected `js/world.js`, `index.html`, `js/util.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/lore.js`, and `js/interiors.js` for integration compatibility.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, and interactables.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

How to Investigate

123:
124:

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

125:

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

126:

Casebook

Tab opens the case file: evidence, suspects, map, the sect, notes. You can fast-travel to known locations from the map.

127:

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

128:

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

129:

Stay human

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State

### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.
