## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State

### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State

### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

How to Investigate

123:
124:

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

125:

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

126:

Casebook

Tab opens the case file: evidence, suspects, map, the sect, notes. You can fast-travel to known locations from the map.

127:

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

128:

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

129:

Stay human

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Casebook

Tab opens the case file: evidence, suspects, map, the sect, notes. You can fast-travel to known locations from the map.

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.
- Test in-browser, fix issues, and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted the hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Confirmed interior implementation passes `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement missing NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`, likely preventing startup.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining world/interior APIs and fix the undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` startup failure.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and unresolved startup call.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, with layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials.
- Interior changes passed `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` has a syntax error: `node --check js/world.js` reports `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input` at line 625.
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and complete `js/world.js`, fixing its syntax error and undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` call.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and startup blockers.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.
- Available browser tools include `playwright-cli`; the repository provides `start.sh` for launching the project.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials; interior changes passed `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` has a syntax error: `node --check js/world.js` reports `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input` at line 625.
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and complete `js/world.js`, fixing its syntax error and undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` call.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and startup blockers.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.
- A subagent was asked to summarize exact world/interior interaction data and NPC data shape; its response was still pending.

## Objective
- Build and verify **THE NINTH HOUR**, a complete, playable psychological horror detective game set in fictional Mercy Falls.

## Requirements
- Implement first-person interaction, persistent NPC/world simulation, non-omniscient killer AI, investigation, procedural cases, and evidence.
- Test in-browser, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide), and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, procedural audio, original lore, and modular JavaScript.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game scaffold, styles, lore, shared utilities, procedural audio, and partial 3D world.
- Implemented 12 interior builders in `js/interiors.js`, including layouts, evidence props, interactables, chapel undercroft geometry, and paired enter/exit portals.
- Adjusted hospital evidence marker, foundry ash, and undercroft medal materials; interior changes passed `node --check` and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Integrate interior scenes with `World`, implement NPC meshes and gameplay systems, and create `js/main.js`.

### Blocked
- `js/world.js` has a syntax error: `node --check js/world.js` reports `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input` at line 625.
- `World` construction calls undefined `_initNpcMeshes()`.
- `index.html` references missing `js/main.js`; gameplay is not implemented or browser-tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and complete `js/world.js`, fixing its syntax error and undefined `_initNpcMeshes()` call.
2. Implement controls, simulation, investigation UI, persistence, procedural cases, and `js/main.js`.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; fix issues and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `js/world.js`: Partial Three.js world implementation and startup blockers.
- `js/interiors.js`: Interior scenes, evidence props, interactables, and portals.
- `js/lore.js`: Setting, locations, cast, and lore data.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities and procedural/random helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `index.html`: Game interface scaffold and module entry point.
- `css/style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `Agents.md` and `index.html` are modified, and `css/` and `js/` are untracked.
- `World` exposes scene, camera, renderer, colliders, interactables, interiors, NPC collections, `isInside`, `currentZone`, and collision helpers. It has no apparent update/render loop API, so `main.js` must own the loop.
- A subagent was asked to summarize exact world/interior interaction data and NPC data shape; its response was still pending.

How to Investigate

Move

W A S D walk, Shift run, mouse to look. Click the scene to capture the cursor. Esc releases it.

125:

Work the scene

Approach the glinting markers and press E. Every piece of evidence is logged to your casebook. Some clues only resolve in the lab.

Casebook

Tab opens the case file: evidence, suspects, map, the sect, notes. You can fast-travel to known locations from the map.

127:

Interviews

Press E on a person. Ask about the victim, the sect, alibis. Present evidence to break a story. People remember how you treat them.

128:

Warrant

Background checks reveal physical traits. Compare them against the lab results, verify alibis, then request a warrant on the Suspects page.

129:

Stay human

Sleep, eat, and keep your stress down. The town does not pause for you, and the killer is watching how you work.

## Integration summary

### `World` and 3D scene

`World` is exported from [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js). Its constructor creates the Three.js scene, camera, and renderer; appends the renderer canvas to `#scene`; initializes world state; builds the outdoor environment and interiors; initializes weather and NPC meshes; and registers a resize handler.

The world state includes:

- `colliders` and `interactables` arrays
- `interactablesById` and `scenes` maps
- `interiors` and `buildingGroups` arrays
- NPC-related fields: `keyNpcs` (`Map`), `genericNpc` (`null` initially), and `genericList` (`[]` initially)
- Environment state including `isInside`, `currentZone`, `rain`, `snow`, `stars`, and lighting/material arrays

**NPC integration is unresolved:** the constructor calls `this._initNpcMeshes()`, but that method and any NPC registration or NPC interactable shape were not found in the inspected source. The fields above do not establish an NPC data contract, so one should not be inferred.

The methods found on `World` are:

- Lifecycle and setup: `constructor`, `resize`, `_initLights`, `_initGround`, `_initRoads`, `_initTown`, `_initProps`, `_initWeather`
- Materials and geometry: `planeMat`, `makeBox`, `makeCylinder`, `makePlane`, `sign`
- Collision: `addCollider`, `addColliderAt`, `collides`
- Buildings and locations: `makeSolidBuilding`, `addWindows`, `frontPos`, `makeEnterable`, `_wall`, `makeOutdoorZone`
- Props and landmarks: `makeHouse`, `makeCar`, `makeCemetery`, `makeRiverbank`, `makeStreetLamp`, `makeTree`, `makeStreetFurniture`

`std` is also exported from this file as a material helper. The constructor calls `buildInteriors(this)` after outdoor props and before weather and NPC setup.

### Interactables and interiors

[`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/interiors.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/interiors.js) registers interactables through a helper that skips an item if its ID is already in `interactablesById`; otherwise, it appends the item to `world.interactables` and indexes it in the map.

The verified **evidence** shape is:

```js
{
  id,          // `${placeId}:${suffix}`
  position,    // THREE.Vector3, computed from the evidence mesh's world position
  label,
  description,
  kind: 'evidence',
  location: placeId,
  object: itemMesh
}
```

The **portal** shape is:

```js
{
  id,                    // `${id}:enter` or `${id}:exit`
  position,              // THREE.Vector3
  destinationPosition,   // cloned THREE.Vector3
  label,
  description,
  kind: 'portal',
  action: 'travel',
  from,
  to,
  location: id
}
```

Portals are registered in pairs: entering travels from the exterior position to the interior position, and exiting reverses the positions and `from`/`to` values. Building portal positions are derived from the location’s door side (`north`, `east`, `west`, or default `south`). Portal IDs and evidence IDs are therefore important for stable lookup and duplicate avoidance.

`buildInteriors(world)` returns without building if the world, scene, or interactables array is missing, or if `_interiorsBuilt` is already set. It initializes `interactablesById` from existing interactables if needed, builds configured locations, and registers interior records. The builders cover the precinct, chapel, library, diner, hospital, bar, motel, foundry, warehouse, victim home, apartment, and chapel basement. The chapel basement also has a specific portal connection to the chapel.

There is no verified general NPC interactable schema in the inspected files.

### Lore data

[`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/lore.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/lore.js) exports:

`GAME_TITLE`, `TOWN`, `LOCATIONS`, `SCENE_ANCHORS`, `KEY_PLACES`, `VICTIM_TEMPLATES`, `CAST`, `SUSPECT_IDS`, `WITNESS_LINES`, `CODEX`, `ENDINGS`, `NEWS_HEADLINES`, `AMBIENT_RADIO`, `GENERIC_LINES`, `GENERIC_JOBS`, and `FLAVOUR_SIGNS`.

`LOCATIONS` provides the shared town layout used by the world and interior builders; its entries include fields such as `name`, `short`, `x`, `z`, `w`, `d`, `h`, `kind`, `color`, `door`, `interior`, and `spot` where applicable.

### Audio API

[`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js) exports `AudioEngine`, a procedural Web Audio implementation. Its methods are:

`init`, `noiseBuffer`, `buildAmbient`, `loopNoise`, `setScene`, `setStress`, `resume`, `setMuted`, `tick`, `footstep`, `heartbeat`, `whisper`, `ui`, `shutter`, `stinger`, `bell`, `thunder`, and `scream`.

### HTML and CSS integration

[`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html) defines the UI and loads [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css). The renderer’s required mount point is `#scene`. The HTML also references `js/main.js` as its module entry point, but that file was not present in the inspected `js/` directory, so the DOM-to-game-controller wiring could not be verified.

Principal DOM contracts include:

- **Scene and overlays:** `#app`, `#scene`, `#fx`, `#flash`, `#dread`, `#fade`
- **HUD and interaction:** `#hud`, `#clock`, `#weather`, `#moon`, `#stress-word`, objective and health/stress/stamina fields, `#crosshair`, `#prompt`, `#prompt-text`, `#interact-progress`, `#toasts`, `#ticker`, `#controls-hint`
- **Casebook:** `#casebook`, `#book-content`, navigation counters and tab controls, page title/stamp/clock/weather fields
- **Dialogue:** `#dialogue`, `#dlg-portrait`, `#dlg-initials`, `#dlg-name`, `#dlg-role`, `#dlg-mood`, `#dlg-trust-bar`, `#dlg-text`, `#dlg-options`, `#dlg-hint`, `#dlg-leave`
- **Title, modals, pause, and ending:** title-screen buttons; help and save/load modal IDs; pause controls and audio/grain options; ending text, stats, and action buttons; `#hint-banner`

The stylesheet sets up the full-screen scene/canvas, HUD and modal layout, overlay effects, and visibility/state styling used by those elements.
